$comment: Authoring for FORM-B (US.59 — Cold War competition in arms, economics and ideology, including the roles of the UN, NATO and the Warsaw Pact). Distractor rationales name the specific misconception each wrong choice catches.

PSTIM-0166.dokRationale: The student recalls the stated purpose of a named treaty organisation. One retrieved fact, which is DOK-1; explaining why a peacetime alliance broke with American tradition would be DOK-2.

B: Free trade among Western nations came through separate economic instruments — the Marshall Plan and later the OEEC. NATO's founding treaty is a mutual-defence pact.
confuses NATO's military purpose with postwar economic cooperation
C: No political union was created. Each member kept full sovereignty; NATO commits members to respond to an attack, not to govern jointly.
reads a defensive alliance as a step toward European political union
D: Several founding members were themselves colonial powers in 1949. Decolonisation was not a NATO aim and in places ran against member interests.
attributes decolonisation aims to an alliance of colonial powers

q-us59-dok1-4.dokRationale: The student recalls what a named term denoted. A single retrieved definition, which is DOK-1.

A: The word 'satellite' here is political, not orbital — it describes a state held in another's orbit of control, and predates the space programme.
reads 'satellite state' as a reference to spaceflight
B: Participation was not voluntary. Soviet troops remained after 1945 and coalition governments were replaced by communist ones, as in Czechoslovakia in 1948.
mistakes imposed control for voluntary partnership
C: Nations receiving American aid were the Marshall Plan recipients in Western Europe — the opposite bloc.
reverses which bloc the satellite states belonged to

PSTIM-0167.dokRationale: The student must connect the fact of the treaty to what it broke with in American practice — a relationship between an event and a tradition, which is DOK-2. Naming the year or the members would be DOK-1.

A: The opposite: Washington's Farewell Address warned against permanent alliances, and the United States had avoided them in peacetime for over 150 years.
reverses the American tradition NATO broke with
B: The treaty carried no expiry. It has been in continuous force since 1949 and has expanded well beyond its original members.
invents a time limit the treaty does not contain
C: Article 5 is precisely a military commitment: an attack on one is treated as an attack on all. That obligation is what made the treaty historically significant.
empties the alliance of the mutual-defence obligation that defines it

U7-DOK2-0005.dokRationale: The student must read two alliance systems as expressions of an ideological contest — inferring a pattern from paired events, which is DOK-2.

B: Both were defence pacts. The economic instruments of the period were separate: the Marshall Plan on one side, COMECON on the other.
confuses the military alliances with the parallel economic blocs
C: They were not created jointly and not at the same time. NATO came in 1949 and the Warsaw Pact in 1955, formed in response to it.
treats two opposing alliances as a cooperative project
D: Disarmament is the reverse of what followed. Both blocs expanded conventional and nuclear forces through the 1950s and 1960s.
reads an arms build-up as an agreement to disarm

q-us6-dok4-cr1.dokRationale: The student must construct and defend an evaluation of why a conflict stayed 'cold', weighing several causes against evidence. Building and defending an argument is DOK-3.
